title: Commit
summary: git commit saves a snapshot of your staged files, with a message, so every version of your project is kept.

levels.title: Your first commit
levels.briefing: A commit is a snapshot of your project at one moment, with a message saying what changed. Each commit points back to the one before it, which is why the history forms a chain in the graph.
levels.objective: Create a file called notes.txt with any text in it, then commit it.

cheatsheet.description: Stage a file for the next commit

hints: First the file has to exist. Create it in the terminal or the file editor.
Stage notes.txt, then commit it with a message.
Run: echo "my notes" > notes.txt, then git add notes.txt, then git commit -m "Add notes"
levels.successMessage: Your commit points back to the README commit, so the graph now shows a chain of two.

levels.title: Two files, one commit
levels.objective: Create todo.txt and ideas.txt, then save both in a single new commit.
hints: A single commit can contain several files.
Stage both files before you commit.
Run: touch todo.txt ideas.txt, then git add todo.txt ideas.txt, then git commit -m "Add lists"
levels.successMessage: A commit saves everything that is staged at that moment.

levels.title: Two separate commits
levels.objective: Commit a.txt on its own, then commit b.txt in a second commit.
hints: Only staged files go into a commit.
Stage and commit a.txt first. Then do the same for b.txt.
Run: git add a.txt, git commit -m "Add a", git add b.txt, git commit -m "Add b"
levels.successMessage: Small, separate commits make the history easier to read.

levels.title: Fix and commit
levels.objective: README.md says "# Helo". Change it to "# Hello" and commit with the message "Fix typo".
hints: Edit the file first, in the editor or with echo.
A changed file must be staged again before committing.
Run: echo "# Hello" > README.md, git add README.md, git commit -m "Fix typo"
levels.successMessage: Changing a committed file and committing again records a new version; the old one is still in the history.
